summary:
ASTROBASE is an interactive 3D Moon-to-Mars colony simulator and space science trainer designed for students ages 7–12+. Addressing the challenge of making real spaceflight engineering trade-offs both tangible and engaging for young learners, the web app puts players in command of a six-person outpost across a 30-day mission at either the Lunar South Pole or Mars’ Jezero Crater.

Starting with 1,000 Credits, students buy and place 13 NASA-inspired modules -including solar arrays, battery banks, MOXIE-style oxygen generators, water extractors, greenhouses, and radiation shields - onto 3D crater terrain. Advancing day-by-day forces learners to balance competing demands across oxygen, water, food, energy, and crew health while responding to realistic hazards like lunar shadow periods, Martian dust storms, and solar flare alerts. Integrated Research Lab unlocks, Space Academy articles, and credit-rewarding quizzes reinforce the real planetary science behind every decision. By transforming abstract resource budgets into hands-on survival choices without requiring installations, ASTROBASE builds early systems-thinking and scientific literacy for the next generation of explorers.
details:
What It Does & How It Works ASTROBASE is an interactive 3D Moon-to-Mars colony simulator and space science trainer built for students ages 7–12+. Players act as mission commanders managing a six-person outpost across a 30-day mission at either the Lunar South Pole or Mars’ Jezero Crater. Starting with 1,000 Credits (CR), players purchase 13 NASA-inspired modules across Energy, Life Support, Agriculture, Protection, and Exploration—such as Solar Arrays, Battery Banks, MOXIE-inspired Oxygen Generators, Water Extractors, Greenhouses, Hydroponics, Radiation Shields, and Surface Rovers.

Using a real-time 3D terrain canvas, players rotate and place modules onto slope-validated crater terrain. Pressing ADVANCE DAY runs a daily simulation cycle that calculates solar power generation, equipment energy consumption, life-support resource usage (Oxygen, Water, Food), radiation exposure, and crew health. Color-coded status bars (Green for Healthy, Yellow for Warning, Red for Critical) give immediate visual feedback. Mid-mission environmental hazards including extended lunar shadow periods, Martian dust storms, solar flare radiation alerts, and equipment malfunctions require strategic trade-offs accompanied by concise science explanations. Players also unlock technologies in the Research Lab, read six articles in the Space Academy, and earn bonus mission credits by completing three interactive 5-question quizzes (Moon Knowledge, Mars Knowledge, and Space Weather).

Benefits & Intended Impact Spaceflight concepts like closed-loop life support, energy storage during long lunar nights, and in-situ resource utilization (ISRU) are often either oversimplified or too technical for young learners. ASTROBASE makes engineering trade-offs tangible and memorable through cause-and-effect gameplay—students see immediately what happens when batteries run empty during an eclipse or when dust reduces solar output. By linking quiz performance directly to in-game mission credits and running entirely in a standard web browser with offline localStorage saving, ASTROBASE provides an accessible, zero-setup STEM learning tool for classrooms, homes, and young aspiring explorers.

Tools, Coding Languages & Scientific References

  • Languages & Frontend: HTML5, CSS3, and Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+).
  • 3D Graphics & Rendering: Three.js (r128) with OrbitControls for procedural crater terrain, dynamic sunlight/shadow casting, Martian atmospheric fog, dust particle systems, and interactive 3D module placement.
  • Storage & Deployment: Browser localStorage for offline progress persistence, deployed publicly via GitHub Pages and Netlify.
  • NASA & Planetary Reference Data: Environmental parameters, hazard mechanics, and Space Academy modules are modeled on the LRO Diviner Lunar Radiometer Data Archive, NASA SVS 4574 (Lunar South Pole Illumination), LPI Lunar South Pole Atlas, NASA PDS Curiosity MSL REMS dataset, Mars 2020 Perseverance (MEDA & MOXIE) documentation, and the NASA DONKI Space Weather Database.

Creativity & Design Considerations

  • Bridging Gameplay and Scientific Honesty: Rather than presenting arbitrary game numbers as real measurements, our team explicitly labeled simulated game-balance parameters while pairing every hazard, research project, and Space Academy article with real planetary science and direct NASA source links.
  • Kid-Friendly Accessibility & UX: We designed a high-contrast dark interface with clear Green/Yellow/Red status indicators, a built-in interactive solar-power slider in the "How to Play" guide, and instant feedback on quiz answers so children ages 7–12+ can learn independently without complex menus or installations.
  • Zero-Friction Architecture: Packaging the entire 3D simulator, simulation engine, and educational academy into a lightweight, self-contained web app ensures smooth performance even on low-power school computers or mobile devices, complete with a toggleable graphics quality setting.
